content.comment_body: Hello, I'm new to programming. A client has given me a [product_name] device, and I've been experimenting with it. Initially, I was able to upload and run the program successfully. Recently, though, I've only been able to create programs or download existing ones from the device. When I connect, the software recognizes the [product_name], but I can't upload new programs. I'm connecting via USB cable and using a device with article number [article_no]. Any ideas what I might be doing wrong?
The quality of the screenshots provided is poor and the message text in the second screenshot is unreadable.
The message on screen says: download from PC to [product_name] failed. Here's the log: *** 12/30/22 3:19 PM Circuit Diagram3 *** PC --> [product_name] Download PC --> [product_name] failed.
Have you selected the correct hardware type in the LSC diagram? Did you set the [product_name] device to transfer mode?

It doesn't work in [version_no] or [version_no]. Yes, I cleared the device memory and enabled transfer mode. I suspect this [product_name] is defective, because another identical device works as expected. Is it common for communication ports to fail when using USB cables?
I'm sorry, but I don't quite understand your question.

[user_name], make sure to select the hardware type for your [product_name] device in the settings. You can find the type displayed in the lower right of the screen and double-click that icon to open the settings.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are experiencing intermittent issues when uploading programs to a [company_name] [product_name] device via USB. While the device and software are detected, uploads are not reliable, particularly with [product_name] software version [version_no]. There are concerns about compatibility between software/hardware or possible hardware defects like faulty communication ports.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect stable and reliable upload/download functionality between their PC and [product_name] module using the provided software and USB connection.
